- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply downward correction by 1–3% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1) and prices are falling, model underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment unit.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.7) and prices are falling, model often fails to recognize the reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment decay, especially if sentiment drops below 0.3 within 3 days.
